page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-48-highlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine tailored for data-intensive enterprise workloads. The instance is powered by an x86_64 processor architecture offering 48 dedicated vCPUs alongside 378.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. This configuration operates without discrete GPU accelerators and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

A primary defining feature of the z4d-highmem-48-highlssd is its substantial integrated local storage array. The server includes six NVMe solid-state drives totaling 22,549 GB of high-speed local disk capacity directly attached to the host. Because these NVMe disks are physically co-located on the hypervisor host, they provide high input/output bandwidth and low disk access latencies for throughput-sensitive processes.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of high-density local NVMe storage and an elevated memory ratio supports cost efficiency by consolidating large-scale I/O workloads onto a single instance. However, operating with ephemeral local SSD storage introduces operational tradeoffs, as local drive data does not persist past instance termination or host events, requiring application-level redundancy strategies.

Given its hardware specifications, Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-48-highlssd is suited for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, high-capacity search indices, operational analytics, and intensive extract, transform, and load processing pipelines.
